# Canonical source parity: fewer planes without changing the parameter

This note uses ACTUAL proper deepest marks, their proved interpolation
rigidity, and the full radial-cone parameter certificate. It is not
about arbitrary concave PL weights or prescribed contact data.

It proves two finite reductions. First, the same sampled parameter has
a representation by at most the occupied-parity count of affine planes,
while retaining the ORIGINAL certificate and all its target rows.
Second, if desired, one can choose a parameter certificate whose source
bases themselves form an empty lattice polytope. Neither statement is
a cap-payment theorem or a way to divide an aggregate surface stress
among the new planes.

## 1. Exact standing inputs

Use the setting and the proved inputs of
candidate 3b257d8ddacb6167
and its independent audit. Thus P=conv(P) intersect Z^n is finite,
K_z are positive compatible d-dimensional fibers, C is their canonical
hull, dm is original mixed volume, M=dm(C), and L>0 is a continuous
concave parameter. Its normalized buffered maximum is attained and
the strict bad-base regime supplies a nonempty finite set J of proper
deepest bases. Each p in J has its unique fiber-interior deepest mark
Y_p=(p,y_p).

Two proved facts will be used explicitly.

(A) If p_i in J, theta_i>0, sum theta_i=1, and
q=sum theta_i p_i is integer, then q is in J and

    Y_q=sum theta_i Y_p_i,
    L(Y_q)=sum theta_i L(Y_p_i).                         (1)

The first fact uses convexity of the real buffered maximum superlevel
and the strict pure-base-depth superlevel. The second uses an attained
own-proper cap at Y_q: every endpoint threshold lies at or below its
exact Q-quantile; averaging and concavity force equality in the
buffer radius, then in L by strict monotonicity of the positive
geometric mean. These are the actual quantile arguments proved in
Sections 6a--6b of the cited source; no new equality hypothesis is
introduced here.

(B) There is a finite positive source measure on these marks,

    mu=sum_(p in J) m_p delta_Y_p,
    nu=dm/(M L),

with

    integral h dmu >= integral h dnu  for every h in T_L,
    T_L={h continuous on C:h+cL is concave for some c>=0}. (2)

Its nonzero coefficients obey m_p=sigma_p/L(Y_p), sum sigma_p=1.
Both signs of affine functions and of L lie in T_L, so

    mu(C)=nu(C),   integral w dmu=integral w dnu,
    integral L dmu=integral L dnu=1.                    (3)

The corresponding actual full-space martingale rows, when used below,
have target nu and are supported on the contact set of EVERY affine
majorant of L that touches their source.

For the first reduction, retain the ORIGINAL mu and its rows. Let
J_+={p:m_p>0} and B=conv(J_+). Lattice points of B belong to J by (1),
but need not belong to J_+.

## 2. The maximal occupied-face cover and its parity count

For a polytope B with integer vertices, call a face Q occupied in its
relative interior if relint Q contains an integer point. Take all
inclusion-maximal such faces Q_1,...,Q_s. Every integer point of B
lies in at least one Q_l: its unique minimal containing face has that
point in its relative interior and can be enlarged to a maximal
occupied face. In particular this covers J_+.

Choose q_l in relint Q_l intersect Z^n. Their parities are pairwise
distinct. Indeed, if q_l and q_m had the same parity, their midpoint
would be integer and would lie in the relative interior of the
smallest face containing Q_l and Q_m. To verify the last statement,
a face containing the midpoint must contain both endpoints (a
supporting affine functional is zero at their strict average only
if zero at each). A face containing q_l contains its minimal face
Q_l, and likewise for Q_m. Thus the minimal face of the midpoint is
exactly this join. It is occupied and strictly larger than either
distinct maximal face, a contradiction.

Every q_l lies in B intersect Z^n, hence in P. Therefore

    s <= k(P) <= 2^n,                                  (4)

where k(P) is the number of occupied integer parity classes of P.
This is a COVER. Its closed faces can overlap on sampled boundary
points; no partition or additive mass identity is asserted.

## 3. One actual plane touches all sources in each covering face

Fix Q=Q_l and q=q_l. The finite source set J_+ intersect Q has convex
hull Q, since the vertices of Q are vertices of B and belong to J_+.
Because q is in relint Q, it has a convex representation using ALL
these source bases with strictly positive weights. The elementary
construction is to take a sufficiently small positive multiple of
their average and express the remaining point of Q as a convex
combination. Property (1) identifies their averaged marks with Y_q
and gives equality of their averaged L-values.

Choose any finite affine majorant A_Q of L on the SAMPLED fibers
touching it at Y_q. Such a majorant exists even at a boundary base:
take a finite continuous-coordinate supergradient c of L(q,.) at
the interior point y_q; the finite sampled support LP supplies a
base slope. This is precisely the proved Farkas construction in
candidate 87de5b3c068291f1,
Section 2. A_Q is positive on all sampled fibers, hence on their
canonical convex hull by affinity.

For every p in J_+ intersect Q,

    A_Q(Y_p)=L(Y_p).                                   (5)

Indeed all these gaps are nonnegative and their strictly positive
weighted average is the zero gap at Y_q, by affinity of A_Q and (1).
Thus each gap is zero. This uses no arbitrary full-space supergradient
at a boundary-base mark.

If actual rows are retained, (5) and their L-Jensen equality imply
that EVERY row with source in J_+ intersect Q is supported on the
sampled equality set {A_Q=L}. It also lies in the convex set

    C intersect {A_Q<=L}.

Here A_Q-L is convex, but need not be nonnegative at unsampled
points; hence its sublevel set, rather than its zero set, is the
justified convex set for the OLD extension. After the replacement
in Section 4, A_Q is a global majorant of V and the new equality
set {A_Q=V} is itself convex. No assertion says that the sum of
these rows is uniform measure on such a set, or that rows for
different Q are disjoint.

## 4. The same sampled parameter has at most k(P) planes

Put

    V=min_(l=1,...,s) A_Q_l.                            (6)

This is a finite positive concave PL function on C. On every sampled
fiber V>=L, while (5) and the covering property give V(Y_p)=L(Y_p)
at every ORIGINAL positive source. Since V is concave, V belongs
to T_L. Test (2) with V and use (3):

    1=integral V dmu >= integral V dnu
       >= integral L dnu=1.

Thus integral(V-L)dnu=0. The target nu has a strictly positive density
relative to ordinary d-volume in every sampled positive fiber.
The continuous nonnegative gap therefore vanishes throughout every
sampled fiber, including its boundary. Consequently

    V=L on C intersect (Z^n x R^d).                    (7)

Equations (4), (6), and (7) prove the claimed at-most-k(P) plane
representation. The original source measure, source marks, target
law, row barycenters, and all sampled parameter values are unchanged.
Every old positive row has zero gap for any new plane touching its
source; this also follows directly because (7) preserves its L-values
and the affine barycenter identity.

The extension between sampled fibers may change. The new V is
nevertheless a legitimate positive concave parameter on C with
identical normalization and buffered values on every mixed point.
If L was an attained optimizing parameter, V has the identical
objective value and is another attained representative. No equality
away from the sampled fibers is asserted.

The new planes are anchored at proper deepest marks Y_q_l whose bases
have distinct parities, although some may have had zero weight in
the original certificate. Uniform source-interiority estimates
therefore apply to these anchors whenever those estimates hold for
ALL proper deepest marks.

The cover is also gradient-consistent. Every positive original source
has a unique continuous gradient of L. Since A_Q touches all sources
in Q, its continuous gradient equals each of theirs. Thus all those
sources have the same gradient label. Every active sampled majorant
at the interpolated mark Y_q touches those sources by the same
averaged-gap argument, so q belongs to the enlarged closed source
class of that label. The distinct-parity witnesses can therefore
be charged within their respective enlarged gradient classes.
Equation (7) preserves continuous gradients almost everywhere in
each full-dimensional sampled fiber, so it also preserves the
original-volume gradient-label mass identities. It still supplies
no disjoint allocation of cap incidences on contact boundaries.

### 4a. The unchanged rows certify the NEW radial cone as well

One must not assume T_V is a subset of T_L: the extensions need not
agree away from the sampled fibers. Instead use the actual old rows.
Write their unnormalized target measures as nu_p, with

    sum_p nu_p=nu,  nu_p(C)=m_p,
    integral w dnu_p=m_p Y_p,
    integral L dnu_p=m_p L(Y_p).

All their support lies in the sampled set. Equation (7) therefore
gives the exact new Jensen equality

    integral V dnu_p=m_p V(Y_p).

For ANY h in T_V, choose c>=0 with h+cV concave. Jensen in the same
row and subtraction of this V equality gives

    integral h dnu_p <= m_p h(Y_p).

Summing proves the unchanged source inequality for every h in the
NEW radial cone T_V. Moreover dm/(M V)=nu on the sampled target,
V(Y_p)=L(Y_p), and the original sigma_p are unchanged.

This observation also supplies the precise bridge when the original
certificate is the parameter component of a specified JOINT linear
body/parameter separator. Retain its original marks, physical cap
law, contact/support allocations, and numerical coefficients.
The sampled L and log L values, and the within-fiber continuous
gradients at all interior marks, are identical for V. Thus every
pure-body response in the existing formulas that uses these
quantities is identical. Its old pure-body inequality is retained.
The preceding row proof supplies the parameter inequality on T_V
with the SAME coefficients. These inequalities add on the joint
cone formed from those admissible pure-body and pure-parameter
directions, exactly as in the original separator construction.

This is a reuse of a specified joint separator, not an inference
that an arbitrary parameter-only certificate has the coefficients
of an independently chosen physical separator. Nor does it identify
unproved body/parameter tangent cones: the pure-body response
formula and the joint-cone decomposition must be those already
established in the application. Under those standing inputs no
new separator, source relabeling, or boundary allocation is needed.

## 5. Optional certificate contraction with all cone inequalities retained

There is also a compact choice of a certificate with parity-distinct
positive source bases. This reduction may change the source weights
and rows, so it is kept separate from Sections 2--4.

Let F be the set of measures mu'=sum_(p in J) m'_p delta_Y_p,
m'_p>=0, satisfying every inequality (2) with the fixed nu.
It is nonempty. Each inequality is closed in the finite coefficient
vector. The tests +/-1 force total mass nu(C), so F is a compact
subset of a finite simplex. The tests +/-L force the L-moment one.
Choose in F a minimizer of integral |w|^2 dmu'.

Suppose two distinct positive atoms have equal-parity bases. Remove
an equal mass epsilon>0 from each and put mass 2epsilon at their
midpoint mark. Property (1) says it is an allowed proper deepest
mark and that its L-value is the endpoint average. For h in T_L
choose c>=0 such that h+cL is concave. Concavity and the exact
L-equality give

    h((Y_1+Y_2)/2) >= [h(Y_1)+h(Y_2)]/2.

Thus every cone inequality (2) is preserved, not merely convex
order or a finite selection of moment constraints. But the quadratic
objective decreases by epsilon |Y_1-Y_2|^2/2>0, a contradiction.
There is at most one positive source base in each occupied parity.

More generally, if a nontrivial positive-weight combination of distinct
positive source bases were integer, remove masses epsilon theta_i
from its atoms and place their sum epsilon at its proper deepest
averaged mark. Property (1) and concavity of h+cL preserve (2) in
exactly the same way, while strict convexity of |w|^2 lowers the
objective. Hence, if J_0 is the resulting positive source set,

    conv(J_0) intersect Z^n = J_0,
    every point of J_0 is a vertex of conv(J_0).          (8)

The source coefficients sigma'_p=m'_p L(Y_p) sum to one.
The same finite-source transport proof as in the standing source
constructs actual full-space rows with target nu and exact L contacts.
This is the archived quadratic contraction mechanism, now with a
proof that the entire ACTUAL radial parameter cone survives it.
It does not assert preservation of unrelated physical surface stress
weights, selected cap laws, or source-specific response coefficients.

## 6. Consequences and remaining gap for rate-cell lifts

Along a sequence of actual canonical attained parameters on a fixed
base, Section 4 permits a sampled representative with at most k(P)
global affine cells at every stage. After a subsequence the number
of planes, their anchor bases, and their distinct-parity pattern can
be fixed. The zero-face rate analysis may use these actual global
cells, retaining all of its coefficient-compactness and nonzero
continuous-gradient hypotheses.

The n=0 two-plane rate example in
candidate 6090c7ee45c2de64
cannot occur in this class. More generally, a generic many-cell
counterexample ignoring the actual source touching constraints does
not refute the canonical statement.

Each ONE global cell with nonzero continuous gradient can use
candidate 185fb6155f830e0e
when its simultaneous slice-limit and interior-base hypotheses hold.
Alternatively one may apply a previously proved lower-continuous-
dimension theorem directly to each actual positive-volume level
slice before taking any limit.

The plane count alone does not allocate the total singular mass
or its selected critical-cap incidence to one inductive center.
Different cells can overlap at sampled boundaries or merge in a
limiting affine-plane group. Their source rows may assign fractional
densities on those contacts. No aggregate inequality is being split
into rowwise or cellwise Gamma payments. Those are separate missing
geometric obligations.
